data.title: Exemplar Luxury Group CEO Says Company Is Stronger After Saks Emerged From Bankruptcy
data.description: Geoffroy van Raemdonck said Exemplar Luxury Group is financially stronger after Saks emerged from bankruptcy, Bloomberg reported. He said customer loyalty, full-price sales and profitable growth helped achieve that goal, supporting reinvestment and stronger relationships with brands.

data.title: Climate Change Outpaces Scientists’ Predictions as COP31 Seeks Emissions Goals
data.description: COP31 aims to set new goals to reduce emissions as climate change outpaces scientists’ predictions and disasters drive billions of dollars in losses, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: Jeff Currie Says China Is Behind His Bearish Copper View
data.description:
Jeff Currie said he is bearish on copper because of China, according to Bloomberg. Currie is CEO and founder of Real Macro and a senior adviser at Carlyle.

In an interview with Vonnie Quinn and Bailey Lipschultz on “The Close,” he said gold’s retreat reflects a shortage of dollar liquidity and discussed the global oil industry.

data.title: Polkadot Community Approves New Strategy With 97% Vote, Prioritizing Product Platform and DotUSD
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher, Polkadot’s decentralized governance system approved a new strategy proposed by the Polkadot Community Foundation (PCF) on November 11, with 97% of votes in favor. The strategy prioritizes the upcoming Polkadot product platform and direct user acquisition, under a mandate confirmed by DOTDAO.

The platform is intended to prioritize user privacy and data rights. PCF plans to launch its first mobile-focused offering through the Polkadot App, supporting private messaging and digital cash payments. The strategy starts its DOT-backed dotStables with dotUSD, designed to track the U.S. dollar and build value for DOT through usage. The Polkadot Technical Fellowship will oversee dotUSD and other dotStables, alongside independent audits and risk management.

The strategy also shifts shared funding and resources away from general marketing toward incentives tied to measurable user engagement. Its stated aim is for product use to drive demand for DOT-backed dotStables, ultimately translating into demand for DOT.

data.title: AI | Match Group CEO Spencer Rascoff Says AI Agents Won’t Date for Users
data.description: Match Group CEO Spencer Rascoff says AI agents will not be allowed to date on behalf of users on Tinder, Hinge and the company’s other apps, which he calls a “human-only zone,” according to Bloomberg. Match uses AI to verify identities, improve safety and block harmful messages. Rascoff discussed where companies should draw the line on AI, how the technology is changing Match Group, Jensen Huang’s departure from Nvidia and why he believes companies are bigger than any one CEO.

data.title: AI | Blackstone-Backed QTS Cuts Planned AI Debt Sale by About 60%
data.description: QTS, a data center operator backed by Blackstone Inc., is reducing the size of a planned private debt sale by about 60% after struggling to attract enough investor demand and refusing to pay much higher yields, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: FAA Halts U.S. Departures Nationwide, Raising Risk for Airline Stocks
data.description: The FAA ordered a nationwide halt to U.S. flight departures after an air traffic control communications failure, raising concerns about airline stocks. The order came around 3:54 p.m. Eastern on Friday, November 13, six minutes before Wall Street closed, according to BeInCrypto. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said communications problems were affecting regional air traffic control centers; the FAA had halted traffic in Chicago shortly before the nationwide order. Aircraft already airborne could continue to land, while international arrivals would be handled individually. Technicians were investigating, with no cause or restart time announced. A Microsoft 365 outage affecting Outlook and Teams since Thursday continued Friday, but no connection to the FAA failure was confirmed. Before the grounding, United Airlines fell 6.0%, American Airlines dropped 5.6% and Delta Air Lines lost 5.2% on Thursday. The Nasdaq fell 0.9% and the S&P 500 declined 0.4% on Friday. The late FAA announcement left little time for a meaningful regular-session market reaction. Extended cancellations could increase airline costs and disrupt schedules, with Monday’s market reopening potentially providing an initial test if the communications problems persist through the weekend.

data.title: US Struggles to Build Affordable Housing as Construction Costs Rise
data.description: Boston Fed Principal Economist and Policy Advisor Paul Willen says soaring construction costs are making many approved housing projects financially unworkable, according to Bloomberg. He points to research showing construction productivity has barely improved in decades, while productivity across much of the rest of the economy has surged.

data.title: BNB Builder Sessions Scheduled for Lima, Rio and Santiago
data.description:
BNB Chain announced on X that BNB Builder Sessions are scheduled in Lima, Rio and Santiago. The Lima meetup is set for Nov 14, described in the post as tomorrow. The Rio session is scheduled for Nov 20, followed by a Santiago meetup on Dec 11. The announcement lists the three cities and dates as separate local gatherings.

The sessions are intended to bring local BNB Chain communities together to learn, exchange ideas and build. BNB Guilds will host the meetups, which are run by builders in each city. The Lima session is next on the schedule, with the Rio and Santiago events taking place afterward on their listed dates. The post identifies BNB Guilds as the host and local builders as the organizers of the city meetups.

data.title: Vanguard CEO Salim Ramji Discusses Career and Altruist Acquisition
data.description:
Barry spoke with Vanguard CEO Salim Ramji about his early career in law, his move to BlackRock as head of corporate strategy and his appointment as Vanguard’s first “outsider” CEO, Bloomberg reported.

They also discussed Vanguard’s recent acquisition of Altruist and its implications for the future of financial advice.

data.title: Microsoft Outage Disrupts Global Commodity Trading
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher, a major Microsoft service outage on Thursday affected government agencies, businesses and traders worldwide, forcing some trading teams to switch to phone calls, fax and instant messaging. The outage added complexity to crude oil trading amid tensions in the Middle East and delayed the release of some commodity price data.

Microsoft said recovery efforts were progressing, but more than 20 products and services could still experience errors.

data.title: Blockstream and Thales Launch Institutional Digital Asset Custody Solution
data.description: According to ChainCatcher, Bitcoin infrastructure company Blockstream and Thales have partnered to launch an institutional digital asset custody solution. Adam Back said offline cold storage can reduce the risk of cyberattacks.

data.title: AI TRENDS | Anthropic Says Error Affecting Microsoft 365 Connector Has Been Resolved
data.description: According to Jin10, Anthropic said the error affecting the Microsoft 365 connector has been resolved.

data.title: U.S. Treasuries Close Mixed as Yield Curve Steepens
data.description:
U.S. Treasuries closed mixed on Friday as the yield curve steepened, with short-term yields falling about 1 basis point and intermediate- to long-term yields rising 2–3 basis points. According to Sina Finance, at 4:23 p.m. New York time, the 2-year yield was down 2.2 basis points at 4.8589%, the 5-year yield was little changed at 4.9706%, the 10-year yield was up 1.4 basis points at 5.1413%, and the 30-year yield had risen 2 basis points to 5.472%.

Just after 3 p.m. New York time, the spread between 2-year and 10-year yields widened by more than 3 basis points. The 10-year yield was around 5.15%, up about 2.5 basis points on the day, after briefly rising above 5.17% for the first time since October 14. Short-term Treasuries reversed earlier losses after U.S. stocks fell, led by Nasdaq 100 constituents.

Long-end swap spreads led gains, closing near their intraday highs and widening nearly 2 basis points on Friday after expanding 1.5 basis points on Thursday. Swaps underperformed Treasuries, and demand for fixed-rate payments may have been related to convexity and contributed to higher yields. Overnight index swaps linked to Fed meeting dates closed little changed, pricing in expectations for about 28 basis points of rate hikes at the December policy meeting. The 5-year/30-year Treasury yield spread rose about 2 basis points to 49.96 basis points, the 2-year/10-year spread widened about 3.7 basis points to 28.03 basis points, and 10-year Treasury futures fell 0.2%.

data.title: STOCKS | US Stocks Close Week Higher Amid Tech Turmoil
data.description: U.S. stocks finished the week higher amid tech turmoil, Bloomberg reported. Bloomberg Television, Bloomberg Radio and YouTube provided cross-platform coverage of the U.S. market close with Vonnie Quinn, Bailey Lipschultz, Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec.

data.title: U.S. Treasury Weighs Bridge Loan to Help Venezuela Repay $2.3 Billion IDB Debt
data.description: According to Jin10, the U.S. Treasury is considering a short-term bridge loan to help Venezuela repay about $2.3 billion in debt owed to the Inter-American Development Bank (IDB) and restore its eligibility for financing. The IDB approved resuming engagement with Venezuela on Friday. After the debt is repaid, Venezuela could receive up to $6 billion in IDB loans over the next two years, while the World Bank could also provide up to $5 billion during the same period. The U.S. plan would provide funds to the IDB through an overnight financing arrangement rather than directly to Venezuela. The proposal could draw attention from Congress. Democratic Senator Elizabeth Warren previously opposed using the Exchange Stabilization Fund to guarantee financial institutions investing in Venezuela.

data.title: International Oil Prices Diverge on the 13th as Light Crude Falls and Brent Rises
data.description: According to Jin10, international oil prices were mixed on the 13th: December-delivery light crude futures on the New York Mercantile Exchange fell 18 cents to $88.56 a barrel, down 0.2%, while January-delivery Brent crude futures rose 2 cents to $95.84 a barrel, up 0.02%.

data.title: STOCKS | Harvest Fund Adds Nvidia in Third Quarter, Keeping It as Its Top Holding
data.description:
An analysis of Harvest Fund’s 13F filing found that it increased its Nvidia holdings in the third quarter, leaving the stock as its largest position and raising its portfolio weighting to 7.1%.

According to Sina Finance, Harvest Fund also added Alibaba and exited its positions in KE Holdings and GDS Holdings.

The analysis covered 463 disclosed investments with a total market value of $3.24 billion. Harvest Fund is one of China’s largest asset managers, and its website reports assets under management of more than RMB 1.8 trillion ($269.8 billion).

data.title: CFTC Chief Seeks Aluminum Pricing Reforms as Costs Rise
data.description: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission chief called for reforms to aluminum pricing, and the agency is examining how prices are set, Bloomberg reported. Aluminum reached a record in the US this year, boosting costs for domestic beverage makers that use the metal in beer and soda cans.
